modules.title: Commercial Banking and Credit Creation
modules.html:
Commercial (Deposit Money) Banks

Financial institutions that accept deposits, lend money and provide payment services for profit.

Accounts
AccountFeatures
CurrentCheque book, no/low interest, overdraft possible
SavingsSmall deposits, earns interest, withdrawal limits
Fixed/time depositFixed sum for a fixed period at high interest
DomiciliaryHeld in foreign currency
Functions
  1. Accepting deposits and safekeeping valuables.
  2. Lending: overdrafts, term loans, discounting bills.
  3. Agency services: standing orders, direct debits, share purchase, executorship.
  4. Foreign exchange, letters of credit, travellers' cheques.
  5. Advisory and cash-management services; issuing cards and e-banking.

Credit Creation

Banks lend most of the money deposited with them, and loans return to the system as fresh deposits. The maximum expansion is given by the credit (bank deposit) multiplier:

$$\text{Credit Multiplier} = \dfrac{1}{\text{Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)}}$$ $$\text{Total Deposits Created} = \text{Initial Deposit} \times \dfrac{1}{\text{CRR}}$$
Limitations on credit creation
  • Level of cash reserve ratio imposed by the CBN
  • Amount of initial/primary deposits
  • Willingness of the public to borrow and to hold cash
  • Availability of good collateral and monetary policy stance

examples.q: A bank receives an initial deposit of ₦2,000,000 and the cash reserve ratio is 20%. Find the credit multiplier and the total deposits that can be created.
If the CBN raises the CRR from 20% to 25%, what happens to the same ₦2,000,000 deposit?
examples.a: \( \text{Multiplier} = \dfrac{1}{0.25} = 4 \), so total deposits fall to \( 2{,}000{,}000 \times 4 = ₦8{,}000{,}000 \). Credit creation shrinks by ₦2,000,000 – this is how a higher CRR tightens money supply and fights inflation.

modules.title: The Central Bank of Nigeria and Monetary Policy
modules.html:
Functions of the CBN

  1. Issue of currency – sole right to print notes and mint coins.
  2. Banker to the government – keeps government accounts, manages public debt.
  3. Banker to other banks – holds their reserves and clears cheques.
  4. Lender of last resort – rescues solvent but illiquid banks.
  5. Custodian of external reserves and manager of the exchange rate.
  6. Regulation and supervision of banks and other financial institutions.
  7. Formulation of monetary policy and promotion of development finance.

Instruments of Monetary Policy

InstrumentHow it works
Open market operationsSale of securities mops up cash; purchase injects cash
Monetary policy rate (MPR)A higher benchmark rate raises the cost of borrowing
Cash reserve ratioHigher CRR reduces lendable funds and the multiplier
Liquidity ratioMinimum liquid assets banks must keep
Selective credit controlDirects credit to priority sectors
Moral suasion & special directivesPersuasion and administrative instruction

Other Institutions

  • Merchant/investment banks – wholesale banking, equipment leasing, issuing houses.
  • Development banks – BOI, BOA, NEXIM, Development Bank of Nigeria.
  • NDIC – insures bank deposits.
  • Microfinance banks, mortgage banks, finance houses, bureaux de change, PFAs.
  • Fintech and mobile money operators – agency banking, payment gateways, USSD transfers.

examples.q: Inflation is rising sharply. Recommend three CBN actions and explain how each works.
examples.a: (1) Raise the MPR – loans become dearer, borrowing and spending fall. (2) Sell treasury bills through open market operations – cash is withdrawn from the banking system. (3) Increase the cash reserve ratio – banks keep more idle cash, the credit multiplier \( \frac{1}{CRR} \) falls and money supply contracts.

examples.q: Distinguish between the CBN and a commercial bank in three ways.
examples.a: Ownership: government-owned vs mainly private shareholders. Motive: monetary stability and regulation vs profit. Customers: government and banks vs the general public. Only the CBN issues currency and acts as lender of last resort.

modules.title: The Capital Market and the Stock Exchange
modules.html:
Money Market vs Capital Market

BasisMoney marketCapital market
PeriodShort term (under 1 year)Medium and long term
InstrumentsTreasury bills, call money, certificates of deposit, commercial papers, bills of exchangeShares, debentures, bonds, mortgages
InstitutionsCBN, commercial & merchant banks, discount housesNGX, SEC, issuing houses, stockbrokers, unit trusts

The Nigerian Exchange (NGX)

A market where existing securities are bought and sold. It has a primary market (new issues – offer for subscription, offer for sale, rights issue, private placement) and a secondary market (trading in existing securities).

Functions
  1. Provides long-term capital for companies and government.
  2. Gives liquidity – investors can convert shares into cash.
  3. Values securities and publishes prices; the All-Share Index measures market performance.
  4. Encourages savings and wider share ownership.
  5. Serves as a barometer of the economy.
Operators
  • Stockbroker – buys and sells on behalf of clients for commission.
  • Jobber/dealer – deals in securities on own account.
  • Issuing house – arranges new issues.
  • Registrar – keeps the register of members and pays dividends.
  • SEC – apex regulator of the capital market.

Useful Formulae

$$\text{Dividend Yield} = \dfrac{\text{Dividend per Share}}{\text{Market Price per Share}} \times 100$$ $$\text{Earnings per Share} = \dfrac{\text{Profit after Tax} - \text{Preference Dividend}}{\text{Number of Ordinary Shares}}$$

examples.q: A company pays a dividend of ₦1.20 per share; the market price is ₦15.00. Compute the dividend yield and interpret it.
examples.a: \( \text{Dividend Yield} = \dfrac{1.20}{15.00}\times100 = 8\% \). An investor buying at ₦15 earns an 8% cash return on the market value, which can be compared with bank interest or treasury-bill rates.

examples.q: Profit after tax is ₦48,000,000, preference dividend ₦8,000,000 and there are 20,000,000 ordinary shares. Find EPS.
examples.a: \( \text{EPS} = \dfrac{48{,}000{,}000 - 8{,}000{,}000}{20{,}000{,}000} = ₦2.00 \) per share – the earnings attributable to each ordinary share, whether distributed or retained.

modules.title: Structure of the Nigerian financial system
modules.html:
Structure of the Nigerian financial system is a key part of The Financial System (SSS 3, Commerce). Master the meaning, the main points and how it is tested in JAMB and WAEC questions on this topic.

Key points

  • Commercial (Deposit Money) Banks Financial institutions that accept deposits, lend money and provide payment services for profit.
  • Credit Creation Banks lend most of the money deposited with them, and loans return to the system as fresh deposits.
  • Regulation and supervision of banks and other financial institutions.
  • Money Market vs Capital Market Basis Money market Capital market Period Short term (under 1 year) Medium and long term Instruments Treasury bills, call money, certificates of deposit, commercial papers, bills of exchange Shares, debentures, bonds, mortgages Institutions CBN, commercial & merchant banks, discount houses NGX, SEC, issuing houses, stockbrokers, unit trusts The Nigerian Exchange (NGX) A market where existing securities are bought and sold.
  • Buyers pay cash to the CBN, so cash leaves the banking system.

Worked example

Q: Deposits in Nigerian banks are insured by
A: NDIC — The Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation protects depositors.

Q: The apex regulator of the Nigerian capital market is
A: SEC — The Securities and Exchange Commission regulates the capital market.

examples.q: Deposits in Nigerian banks are insured by
examples.a: NDIC — The Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation protects depositors.

examples.q: The apex regulator of the Nigerian capital market is
examples.a: SEC — The Securities and Exchange Commission regulates the capital market.

quiz.solution: Existing shareholders may buy new shares in proportion to their holding.

quiz.solution: Only the central bank issues legal tender.

quiz.q: Raising the monetary policy rate generally
quiz.solution: Higher benchmark rates raise lending rates and dampen credit demand.

quiz.q: The secondary market deals in
quiz.solution: Previously issued securities are traded there, giving investors liquidity.

quiz.q: An advantage of listing on the stock exchange is
quiz.solution: Listing allows a company to raise substantial long-term funds from the public.

quiz.q: A market for short-term loans and financial instruments like Treasury Bills is the _____ market.
quiz.solution: The money market deals with high-liquidity financial assets with a maturity of one year or less.

quiz.q: The automated system that allows customers to withdraw cash outside banking hours is the _____.
quiz.solution: Automated Teller Machines (ATMs) provide 24/7 access to basic banking services.

quiz.q: In computer technology, the physical components of the system are called _____.
quiz.solution: Hardware refers to the tangible parts of a computer, such as the monitor, keyboard, and CPU.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a function of the Central Bank of Nigeria?
quiz.solution: The Central Bank has the sole authority to issue and manage the national currency (Naira).

quiz.q: The 'Money Market' is a market for _____.
quiz.solution: The money market deals with financial assets that have a maturity period of one year or less, such as treasury bills.

quiz.q: The Central Bank is responsible for:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Issuing currency.

quiz.q: Which of these is a function of the Central Bank?
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Issuing currency.

quiz.q: Central Bank is:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Lender of last resort.

quiz.q: The central bank function of 'Lender of Last Resort' applies to...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Commercial banks.

quiz.q: The Central Bank is the:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2025). Correct answer: Lender of last resort.

quiz.q: A market where money is lent for short periods is:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2025). Correct answer: Money market.

quiz.q: Central Bank:
quiz.solution: Past question (NECO 2025). Correct answer: Regulates banks.

quiz.q: Commercial Bank:
quiz.solution: Past question (NECO 2025). Correct answer: Accepts deposits.

quiz.q: The abbreviation 'PLC' after a company's name in Nigeria stands for _____.
quiz.solution: PLC denotes a Public Limited Company, whose shares can be bought and sold by the general public on the stock exchange.

quiz.q: A bank draft is safer than a personal cheque because _____.
options: it is signed by the President
payment is guaranteed by the bank
quiz.solution: A bank draft is drawn by the bank on its own funds, so there is no risk of it 'bouncing' due to insufficient funds.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a function of the Nigerian Export Promotion Council (NEPC)?
quiz.solution: The NEPC is the government agency responsible for promoting and diversifying Nigeria's export trade away from oil.

quiz.q: An insurance policy that covers a ship and its cargo against risks on a specific journey is a _____.
quiz.solution: A voyage policy provides cover for a specific route or journey rather than a specific period of time.

quiz.q: A market where commodities are bought and sold for immediate delivery is the _____.
quiz.solution: In a spot market, transactions are settled 'on the spot' with immediate physical delivery of the commodity.

quiz.q: Which type of insurance policy covers a ship's hull and machinery?
quiz.solution: Marine Hull insurance specifically covers the physical structure and equipment of the vessel.

quiz.q: The fee paid periodically to an insurance company to maintain a policy is the _____.
quiz.solution: The premium is the consideration paid by the insured for the protection provided by the insurer.

quiz.q: A market where a single buyer dominates the market for a product is a _____.
quiz.solution: Monopsony occurs when there is only one buyer, giving that buyer significant power over sellers.

quiz.q: Which insurance policy covers employees against injury at work?
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Workmen's Compensation.

quiz.q: A market where new shares are issued is:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Primary market.

quiz.q: Which sector does banking belong to?
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Tertiary/Commercial.

quiz.q: Bull market means prices are:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Rising.

quiz.q: A credit note is issued to a customer when...
options: Goods are returned due to damage
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Goods are returned due to damage.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a function of money?
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Medium of exchange.

quiz.q: Market segmentation involves...
options: Dividing a market into distinct groups of buyers
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Dividing a market into distinct groups of buyers.

quiz.q: Nationalization is the policy where...
options: Private businesses are sold to the public
The government takes over the ownership of a private industry
Foreigners are allowed to buy local shops
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: The government takes over the ownership of a private industry.

quiz.solution: Past question (NECO 2025). Correct answer: Wealth for production.
